literal: The day after Gaozu had some recovery.
idiomatic: The next day Gaozu showed some improvement.

literal: From Xuanchi they favored Ye; Xie constantly attended beside the carriage day and night without leaving the side; he always tasted food and drink first and then with his own hand presented them to the emperor.
idiomatic: From Xuanchi the court favored Ye. Xie never left the carriage day or night, tasted every meal and drink first, and only then served the emperor with his own hands.

literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital they met the hundred officials in the Hall of Proclaiming the Ultimate and performed the ritual of drinking to the end and recording merit.
idiomatic: Back in the capital the court met the hundred officials in the Hall of Proclaiming the Ultimate and performed the rite of drinking to the end and recording merit.

literal: They ordered the palace attendant to proclaim the intent: "Xie assisted and supported the six armies, gathered the weapons in Jing-Chu; on the northern Mian his merit each time joined the temple's plans.
idiomatic: A palace attendant proclaimed: "Xie assisted the six armies and gathered arms in Jing-Chu. North of the Mian his merit joined every plan of the temple."

literal: Following the campaign against Xinye he had the stratagem to take the city;
idiomatic: "On the Xinye campaign he devised how to take the city;"

literal: receiving command at Dengcheng he achieved the effect of a great victory.
idiomatic: "at Dengcheng he won the great victory."

literal: His merit was foremost among the host of generals.
idiomatic: "His merit stands first among the generals."

literal: Separately he should receive reward without diminishing his service.
idiomatic: "He shall be rewarded apart without diminishing his service."

literal: " Gaozu said to Xie: "I with you and the others early suffered hardship; in the middle we met separation; I have often said affection follows affairs and grows thin.
idiomatic: Gaozu told Xie, "You and I early knew hardship, then separation. I have often said affection thins with circumstance."

literal: Recently, bound by illness for a year, perilous as a cold leaf—if not for your deep kin feeling and thick loyalty and filial piety, who could move and stop in person and first taste medicine and food?
idiomatic: "Lately, a year in illness, perilous as a leaf in frost—without your deep kinship and loyal filial piety, who could attend in person, tasting medicine and food before me?"

literal: Each time I trace this affair my moved thought is especially far.
idiomatic: "Each time I recall it my gratitude goes very deep."

literal: " Xie wept and replied: "Your subjects long suffered an untimely heaven and bitterly resent a long lifetime; relying on Your Majesty's fostering we were able to join the ranks of men.
idiomatic: Xie wept and answered, "We long suffered heaven's cruelty and bitterly resent long life. Only by Your Majesty's fostering did we join the ranks of men."

literal: Who would have said the upper spirit had no mirror and again made the holy person depart from harmony—the ten thousand states hang on it, the dark masses tie their breath to it.
idiomatic: "Who thought heaven had no mirror and would again make the holy person ill—the realm hangs on it, the people tie their breath to it."

literal: The labor of lying down and rising—how could it express bitter thoroughwort?
idiomatic: "Our labor waking and sleeping cannot express our bitter thoroughwort."

literal: " For merit in breaking Huijing and the others, fief increased by five hundred households.
idiomatic: For breaking Huijing and the rest his fief was increased by five hundred households.

literal: Again an edict said: "My form was weary from tender years and my heart labored through long years; accumulated thought became illness and suddenly broke out at Ru and Ying.
idiomatic: An edict said, "My body was weary from youth and my heart labored through long years. Thought piled into illness and suddenly broke out at Ru and Ying."

literal: The sixth younger brother Xie—filial piety equal to Zhou's younger brother, feeling comparable to the Duke of Zhou, leaving food and abandoning sleep, in movement and rest always in person, urging the physician and encouraging food—with loyal strength utterly spent he brought this preservation and health; truly it relied on shared breath.
idiomatic: "My sixth brother Xie's filial piety matched Zhou's brother; his feeling matched the Duke of Zhou. He left food and sleep, was always in person, urged physicians and pressed food, spent himself utterly, and brought this recovery. It truly rested on shared breath."

literal: Again he held affairs and governed together; the hundred offices relied on him; net and warp weighed and balanced; the ten thousand measures obtained completion.
idiomatic: "He also held government together; the hundred offices relied on him; he weighed the net and warp; the ten thousand measures were settled."

literal: He pacified the armies in the season of great rain and handled arms on the day of repeated omens.
idiomatic: "He pacified armies in seasons of flood and handled arms on days of ill omen."

literal: Securing the outer and quieting the inner—the great way of a meritorious minister.
idiomatic: "Securing the outer and quieting the inner—that is a great minister's way."

literal: The achievement of attending and guarding within can make deep kin feeling without praise;
idiomatic: "Attendance at the bedside needs no praise for deep kin feeling;"

literal: the diligence of assisting and brightening is truly merit that preserves altars and grain.
idiomatic: "but assisting and brightening is merit that preserves the altars."

literal: There should be recompense and reward to mark the state's merit; fief may increase by one thousand households.
idiomatic: "There should be reward to mark the state's debt. Increase his fief by one thousand households."

literal: " Xie declined and said: "Your subject received encounter through kin; glory and withering are equal in the affair; to obtain reward on this account is especially contrary to feeling and wish; I beg to pursue and complete the former intent to still slander's words.
idiomatic: Xie declined: "I was favored through kinship; glory and decline are one affair. Reward on this account goes against my wish. I beg to restore the former intent and still slander."

literal: " An edict said: "You in private can be filial; in public you must be loyal; recently your diligent care is enough to spread through court and countryside—only reverently receive it.
idiomatic: The edict read, "In private you are filial; in public you are loyal. Your recent care fills court and countryside. Only receive it."

literal: " Soon Xie was made Minister of Works and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Palace Attendant as before.
idiomatic: Soon he was made minister of works and grand tutor of the heir apparent while remaining palace attendant.

literal: Before long Xiao Baojuan was about to have Chen Xianda invade from within; Gaozu again personally campaigned against him.
idiomatic: Before long Xiao Baojuan was to have Chen Xianda invade from within, and Gaozu again took the field in person.

literal: An edict made Xie Bearer of the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, and overall commander of the six armies.
idiomatic: Xie was made bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs within and without, and overall commander of the six armies.

literal: At that time Gaozu was unwell.
idiomatic: Gaozu was then unwell.

literal: Xie declined and said: "Your subject attends illness without leisure; the six armies must have someone to rely on; the affair cannot rise in two places and feeling and strength are again exhausted.
idiomatic: Xie declined: "I attend his illness without rest. The six armies need another hand. Two burdens cannot rise together, and my strength is spent."

literal: I further request one prince to overall hold the military key.
idiomatic: "I beg another prince to hold the military command."

literal: " Gaozu said: "Military affairs and attending illness both rely on you.
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Military affairs and his sickbed both rest on you."

literal: Bound by illness like this—I deeply fear it will not succeed.
idiomatic: "Bound by illness as I am, I deeply fear I will not recover."

literal: To secure the six armies and preserve altars and grain—apart from you, on whom?
idiomatic: "To secure the six armies and preserve the realm—apart from you, whom?"

literal: How can you for convenience request another person and thereby go against the heart's entrustment?
idiomatic: "How can you for convenience ask another and betray what my heart entrusts?"

literal: What the ancestral temple relies on is only in you.
idiomatic: "The ancestral temple relies on you alone."

literal: Zhuge Kongming and Huo Zimeng, of different surname, received entrustment—how much more you!
idiomatic: "Zhuge Kongming and Huo Zimeng were entrusted though of different surname—how much more you!"

literal: " When they halted at Yuyang Gaozu said to Xie: "My illness turns worse; you must exert yourself.
idiomatic: At Yuyang Gaozu told Xie, "My illness grows worse. Exert yourself."

literal: " When the imperial carriage reached Horse Pen, several li from the bandits' camp, Xianda and the others came out to battle and the generals utterly defeated them.
idiomatic: At Horse Pen, a few li from the enemy camp, Xianda came out to fight and the generals broke him utterly.

literal: Xie disposed the various armies and was about to attack the bandits' ramparts; that night they fled in defeat.
idiomatic: Xie disposed the armies to storm the enemy ramparts; that night they fled.

literal: Gaozu's illness was severe; he said to Xie: "Xiu's life is short; death and life are a great division; now my breath and strength are critically weak and will surely not succeed.
idiomatic: Gaozu's illness was grave. He told Xie, "Xiu's life is short; death and life are a great divide. My breath is failing and I will not recover."

literal: Though Xianda is defeated, the state's safety and peril hang on this one throw; what the altars rely on is only in your person.
idiomatic: "Though Xianda is beaten, the state's safety hangs on this one throw. The altars rely on you alone."

literal: Huo Zimeng received charge though of different surname—how much more you, kin and worthy; can you not exert yourself!
idiomatic: "Huo Zimeng took charge though of different surname—how much more you, kin and worthy. Exert yourself!"

literal: " Xie wept and said: "A scholar in plain cloth still exhausts life for one who knows him; how much more your subject, entrusted with spirit by the Former Emperor and linked in splendor with Your Majesty—truly he should exhaust the strength of arms and legs and add loyalty atop it.
idiomatic: Xie wept: "A man in plain cloth still dies for one who knows him. I was entrusted by the Former Emperor and shine beside Your Majesty. I should spend my limbs and add loyalty."

literal: But your subject goes in and out at the throat and gullet and each time crosses the timely key; reaching the splendor of favor and spiritual grace, it is heard far and near.
idiomatic: "Yet I pass through the throat of power and each time cross the timely post. Favor has grown radiant and is heard far and near."

literal: Again participating as chief craftsman, machine and government entirely return; the sound that shakes the ruler—being envied is certain.
idiomatic: "Again I share the chief craft; machine and government all return to me. The sound that shakes the ruler is sure to be envied."

literal: This is precisely the Duke of Zhou's flight in concealment and King Cheng's doubt; Your Majesty loves your subject and then has not yet completed the beauty of beginning and end.
idiomatic: "This is the Duke of Zhou in flight and King Cheng in doubt. Your Majesty loves me yet has not completed the beauty of beginning and end."

literal: Your subject is not therefore hating glory and casting off power, not therefore declining diligence and requesting ease—he only hopes to look up and complete Your Majesty's mirror-bright day and below to mind this foolish subject's forgetting to withdraw and its calamity.
idiomatic: "I do not hate glory or cast off power, nor decline diligence to seek ease. I only hope to complete Your Majesty's mirror-bright day above and spare me the calamity of forgetting to withdraw below."

literal: " Gaozu was long silent and said: "I have pondered your words; the principle truly cannot be wrested away.
idiomatic: Gaozu was silent a long while. "I have pondered your words. The principle cannot be wrested away."

literal: " He then personally wrote an edict to Shizong saying: "Your sixth uncle Xie—pure regulation and splendid reward, with white clouds equally clean;
idiomatic: He then wrote Shizong by his own hand: "Your sixth uncle Xie keeps pure regulation and splendid reward, clean as white clouds;"

literal: weary of glory and casting off the sash, with pine and bamboo as heart.
idiomatic: "weary of glory and casting off rank, with pine and bamboo for a heart."

literal: I from youth was intimate with him and led him in the way's intent.
idiomatic: "From youth I was intimate with him and led him in the way."

literal: Each time he requested to remove the court sash and dwell in true hills and ravines—I, because of the weight of elder brother, could not bear to part far.
idiomatic: "Each time he asked to leave court and dwell in true hills I, as elder brother, could not bear to let him go far."

literal: How can he still be bent to plain vocation and long entangled in the age's net?
idiomatic: "How can he still be bent to plain vocation and long entangled in the world's net?"

literal: After my hundred years listen to Xie resign the cicada and cast off the crown and follow his pure restraint's nature.
idiomatic: "After my hundred years let Xie resign rank and crown and follow his pure restraint."

literal: Do not let the court of King Cheng turn and doubt the Duke of Zhou's sagehood—is that not good?
idiomatic: "Do not let King Cheng's court turn and doubt the Duke of Zhou's sagehood. Is that not good?"

literal: You as filial son—do not disobey my command."
idiomatic: "You are a filial son. Do not disobey my command."

literal: When Gaozu passed away at the traveling palace they restrained and concealed the mourning; Xie alone with Right Vice Director, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, and a few at left and right made plans, conveying Gaozu into the comfort carriage; Xie and the others went in and out as on ordinary days, viewing illness and advancing food; outside memorials could be decided.
idiomatic: When Gaozu died at the traveling palace they concealed the mourning. Xie alone with Right Vice Director Prince Cheng of Rencheng and a few close attendants laid plans, moved Gaozu into the comfort carriage, and went in and out as on ordinary days, still attending illness and serving food while deciding outside memorials.

literal: After many days they reached Wancheng; then at night they advanced the comfort carriage into the commandery hall, were able to add the inner coffin, and returned carrying the lying carriage.
idiomatic: After many days they reached Wancheng. At night they brought the comfort carriage into the commandery hall, enclosed the coffin, and returned in the lying carriage.

literal: Within and without the six armies none knew.
idiomatic: Inside and outside the six armies, no one knew.

literal: They sent Palace Attendant Zhang Ru with an edict to summon Shizong to join the carriage.
idiomatic: They sent palace attendant Zhang Ru with an edict to summon Shizong to join the carriage.

literal: When the coffin reached Luyang they then issued mourning and put on mourning garments.
idiomatic: When the coffin reached Luyang they issued mourning and put on mourning dress.

literal: When Shizong took the throne Xie knelt and handed over several sheets of Gaozu's testamentary command.
idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne Xie knelt and handed over Gaozu's testamentary sheets.

literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi suspected Xie of rebellion and halted outside Luyang commandery; after a long time he then entered.
idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang suspected Xie of rebellion and halted outside Luyang a long time before entering.

literal: He said to Xie: "You are not only toilsome—you are also perilous to the extreme.
idiomatic: He told Xie, "You were not only toilsome—you were perilous to the extreme."

literal: " Xie resented it and replied: "Elder brother's understanding is high and years long—therefore you know there is peace and peril; Yanhe grasps a snake and rides a tiger and does not feel hardship.
idiomatic: Xie answered with resentment, "Elder brother's understanding is high and your years are long, so you know peace and peril. Yanhe grasped a snake and rode a tiger and felt no hardship."

literal: " Xi said: "You resent that I arrived late!
idiomatic: Xi said, "You resent that I came late!"

literal: " From when Gaozu was unwell Xie constantly was at the center, personally attending medicine; day and night he did not leave left and right; reaching to garments and belt rarely unfastened, disordered hair and dirty face.
idiomatic: From Gaozu's illness Xie constantly attended at the center, personally tending medicine day and night without leaving his side, rarely unfastening belt or garments, hair disordered and face unwashed.

literal: The emperor's long illness had many angers and thereby shifted anger onto others.
idiomatic: The emperor's long illness bred many angers, and he turned them on those around him.

literal: Xie was each time scolded and reviled; words reached severity; authority reproached close attendants and movement was about to behead.
idiomatic: Xie was often scolded in words severe enough to kill; authority fell on attendants and death followed.

literal: Xie received the expression with full heart and in many cases corrected and aided.
idiomatic: Xie bore the face with full heart and in many cases corrected and aided.

literal: When Gaozu ascended to the far journey Chen Xianda had just begun to flee in defeat; they feared the evil news would leak and there would be pressing force.
idiomatic: When Gaozu ascended the far journey Chen Xianda had just begun to flee; they feared the evil news would leak and bring pressing force.

literal: Within Xie though grieved and moved, without he showed auspicious expression; in going out and coming in, bowing and looking up, divine appearance was without difference.
idiomatic: Within, Xie grieved; without, he showed an auspicious face. In going out and coming in, bowing and looking up, his divine bearing never changed.

literal: When they reached Luyang also, the Eastern Palace's official attendants mostly suspected Xie of a different intent and secretly harbored guard and fear.
idiomatic: At Luyang also, the Eastern Palace's officers mostly suspected Xie of different intent and secretly guarded against him.

literal: Yet Xie pushed sincerity to the utmost in ritual and in the end had not the slightest fault.
idiomatic: Yet Xie pushed sincerity to the utmost in ritual and in the end showed not the slightest fault.

literal: Xie submitted Gaozu's posthumous-title deliberation: "Respectfully according to the law of posthumous titles: harmonizing the times and inaugurating enjoyment is called 'Filial'; securing the five kindreds is called 'Filial'; virtue broadly heard is called 'Cultured'; threading heaven and earth is called 'Cultured.' Looking up and considering the late emperor, the meaning truly covers these; the honored title should be Emperor Filial Cultured; temple name Gaozu; tomb name Long Mound.
idiomatic: Xie submitted Gaozu's posthumous-title deliberation: "According to the law of posthumous titles, harmonizing the times and securing the five kindreds is 'Filial'; virtue broadly heard and threading heaven and earth is 'Cultured.' The late emperor's meaning truly covers these. The honored title should be Emperor Filial Cultured; temple name Gaozu; tomb name Long Mound."

literal: " Shizong followed it.
idiomatic: Shizong approved.

literal: After the burial Shizong firmly made Xie chief minister.
idiomatic: After the burial Shizong pressed Xie to serve as chief minister.

literal: Xie repeatedly spoke to his face of the testamentary intent and requested to follow his plain wish.
idiomatic: Xie repeatedly cited the testament and asked to follow his plain wish.

literal: Shizong toward Xie was grieved and moved and each time did not permit it.
idiomatic: Shizong, grieving toward Xie, each time refused.

literal: Xie repeatedly submitted memorials and spoke; the words and meaning were earnest.
idiomatic: Xie repeatedly memorialized in earnest words.

literal: Shizong found it hard to go against the testamentary command and followed his elegant wish; still he pressed him with an outside post; therefore he made Xie Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander of Military Affairs in Ji, Ding, You, Ying, and Anping's seven provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Opener of the Office, and Governor of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: Shizong could not override the testament yet wished to honor his elegance; still pressing an outside post, he made Xie bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander of military affairs in the seven provinces of Ji, Ding, You, Ying, and Anping, grand general of agile cavalry, opener of the office, and governor of Dingzhou.

literal: Xie still memorialized decline and again spoke to his face the former intent; Shizong firmly held and did not permit; he then took up his post.
idiomatic: Xie still declined and spoke his former intent to his face; Shizong firmly refused; he then took up his post.

literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su and others memorialized: "Your subjects have heard that displaying merit and marking virtue—the way esteems former kings;
idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su and others memorialized: "We have heard that to display merit and mark virtue is the way of former kings;"

literal: merit for service, kin for kin—the meaning is lofty in great canon.
idiomatic: "merit for service and kin for kin is lofty in great canon."

literal: Therefore the Duke of Zhou assisted Zhou and brightly dwelt at Qufu;
idiomatic: "Therefore the Duke of Zhou assisted Zhou and brightly dwelt at Qufu;"

literal: the Eastern Prince governed Han and favor surpassed the array of feudatories.
idiomatic: "the Eastern Prince governed Han and favor surpassed the feudatories."

literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie—bright thought within, heroic wind without, harmonizing and broadening Qian's regulation, sweeping the vapors of Han and Mian.
idiomatic: "Prince Xie of Pengcheng's bright thought shines within and heroic wind without; he harmonized Qian's regulation and swept the vapors of Han and Mian."

literal: When the Former Emperor was in Heaven the phoenix banner turned its staffs; he quieted the six armies in one and solemnly pacified the southern submission.
idiomatic: "When the Former Emperor was in Heaven the phoenix banner turned homeward; he quieted the six armies at once and solemnly pacified the south."

literal: He set the sage emperor on the heavenly ford and opened the spiritual blessing of Great Wei; deliberating the way at the center pivot, royal plans thereby became solemn; the seven virtues greatly proclaimed, the nine achievements in song.
idiomatic: "He set the sage emperor on the heavenly ford and opened Great Wei's blessing; deliberating the way at the center, royal plans grew solemn; the seven virtues were proclaimed and the nine achievements sung."

literal: Your subjects jointly examined and deem fit to increase fief by one thousand five hundred households.
idiomatic: "We jointly examined and deem his fief should increase by one thousand five hundred households."

literal: " An edict said: "Having read the memorial, doubled grief at the collapse—still not enough to repay merit and virtue on high; for the time being, as memorialized.
idiomatic: The edict read, "Reading the memorial doubles my grief at the collapse—still not enough to repay his merit. For now, as memorialized."

literal: " Xie repeatedly memorialized firm decline; Shizong permitted it.
idiomatic: Xie repeatedly memorialized firm decline; Shizong permitted it.

literal: Shizong wrote to Xie: "Since parting at the farewell I have been choked with grief; years and months easily far—already pressing toward late winter; each time I think of hearing the way I receive and follow the wind's teaching.
idiomatic: Shizong wrote Xie: "Since our farewell grief has choked me. Months slip away and late winter presses. I think constantly of hearing your teaching and following your way."

literal: Father has already resigned glory and rests outside; I cannot for a moment suddenly go against utmost virtue.
idiomatic: "Father has resigned glory and rests apart; I cannot for a moment go against utmost virtue."

literal: Going out to the feudatory many months—the desolation of parting is truly deep.
idiomatic: "You have been in the feudatory many months—the desolation of parting is deep."

literal: Now I send Chief Clerk Liu Daobin to convey grief and longing; I wish Father to come and look—surely he will reach the capital.
idiomatic: "Now I send chief clerk Liu Daobin with my grief and longing. I wish Father to come and look—surely you will reach the capital."

literal: To unfold and release sorrow's end—the finger does not say far.
idiomatic: "To unfold sorrow's end—the day is not far."

literal: " Xie then attended court at the capital.
idiomatic: Xie then came to court at the capital.

literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Xiao Baojuan's Yuzhou Inspector Pei Shuye with Shouyang submitted to the inner; an edict made Xie Commander of All Armies on the Southern Expedition, other offices as before, and with Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su to welcome Shouyang.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingming, Xiao Baojuan's Yuzhou inspector Pei Shuye submitted Shouyang to the inner. Xie was ordered commander of all armies on the southern expedition with other offices unchanged, and with Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su to welcome Shouyang.
